text.p: Pakistan started their short tour of Australia badly on Friday when they were beaten by 13 runs by the Australian Cricket Academy in a limited overs match.
The Academy, coached by former Australia wicketkeeper Rod Marsh, set the visitors a difficult target after scoring 248 for five from 50 overs.
Pakistan started their run chase confidently to reach 161 for two. Acting captain and opener Saeed Anwar scored 56 and number three Zahoor Elahi 61.
The loss of number five Inzamam-ul-Haq for three proved to be a turning point, with Pakistan crumbling badly to lose their last six wickets for 38 runs.
Fast bowler Adam Smith dismissed Zahoor, Ejaz Ahmad for 29 and then Inzamam to finish with three for 40 from 10 overs. Justin Poole and Jeremy Allen took two wickets each.
Pakistan arrived on Wednesday to play in the World Series limited overs tournament against Australia and West Indies, with five other matches against lesser sides also scheduled.
The visitors decided to rest captain Wasim Akram and pace bowling partner Waqar Younis from the Academy match ahead of their first World Series match against Australia on Sunday.
Pakistan missed the experience of Wasim and Waqar as the eager young Academy players started confidently after being put in.
Opener Michael Dighton and Brad Haddin put on 103 for the first wicket, Dighton scoring 62 before he was run out and Haddin 45 before he fell to Saqlain Mushtaq.
Captain Simon Katich and middle-order batsmen Dominic Thornley and Shawn Craig all scored over 30 to help the Academy build a competitive total.
Marsh's young Academy players beat West Indies by eight wickets in a limited overs match a year ago.
